newsitem.title: FRANCE: MATIF plans 5-yr bond future launch June-Sep 1997.
newsitem.headline: MATIF plans 5-yr bond future launch June-Sep 1997.

text.p: French futures and options exchange MATIF SA said on Wednesday it planned to launch a five-year bond futures contract between June and September 1997 as part of its strategy to position itself for the introduction of a single currency.
"It's certain, we know we will do it," Jacques Werren, MATIF deputy managing director, told a news conference.

"Now we have to solve and tackle important issues" such as the appropriate coupon for the notional bond underlying the contract and the basket of bonds eligible for delivery when the futures contract expires, he said.

He said the timing of the launch was very important and that most market participants would prefer to wait until the recently modified long-bond contract had become liquid before issuing the five-year contract.
He said that would be "June 1997...maybe September."

In a report published on Wednesday, a MATIF working committee on the changeover to the euro, said while it expected the five-year contract to be launched between June and September 1997, an early launch should not be excluded.
"In the view of some members of the working committee, the possibility of launching the five-year contract at the beginning of 1997 should not be ruled out," the report said.
"At all cost, a launch at the wrong moment must be avoided: the danger is that investors' current interest in five-year may switch to a longer segment of the yield curve," it said.

MATIF modified recently cut the coupon of the notional bond underlying its long-bond future and lengthed its maturity to between 8.5 and 10.5 years. The aim was partly to make the contract a real 10-year product, leaving space for a five-year contract to be launched.
The working committee envisaged a five percent coupon for the five-year contract and a maturity of 3.5 to 5.5 years. It expected both BTANs and OATs to be eligible for delivery.
The members said options should be launched on the contract, based on the market-making system currently used for options on the long-bond contract.
The report said MATIF had been asked to consider launching a 30-year bond contract although it was unlikely to happen soon.

"While it would be premature to launch this type of product at the moment -- there is no demand today for such a duration -- it could become interesting in the euro context, in particular in relation to the U.S. 30-year contract," the report said.
